answer: An agent marketplace requires each active seller to lock 100 credits in escrow for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Agents named sparrow, jade, and zephyr each need a separate deposit; the same credits cannot back multiple identities. An attacker spawning 1,000 sellers must therefore immobilize 100,000 credits for a month, sacrificing liquidity and interest. Fake identities remain possible, but scaling them demands proportional capital.
